notes: signature.return and signature.params describe the ground-truth C shape,
classified only by width and pointer-ness: '32' means a 32-bit scalar,
'ptr' a pointer, '64' a 64-bit scalar. Signedness is deliberately not
checked -- recovering it reliably needs more evidence than a single
function body carries, and a wrong guess reads worse than an honest
unsigned. Width and pointer-ness are both recoverable, so both are held to.

cases.name: eval_add_three
cases.source: int32_t eval_add_three(int32_t a, int32_t b, int32_t c)

cases.name: eval_rotr32
cases.comment: A rotate is emitted as the rotr32 helper (defined once in xdec_helpers.h), which is the honest spelling of one: C has no rotate operator, and open-coding the shift pair would be longer and no clearer.

cases.name: eval_clamp
cases.source: int32_t eval_clamp(int32_t x, int32_t lo, int32_t hi)

cases.name: eval_sum_array
cases.source: int32_t eval_sum_array(const int32_t* arr, size_t n)
cases.comment: The source counts i up to n; -O1 counts n down instead and branches on the flags the decrement sets, so there is no `i < n` in the machine code and no relational compare to recover. What is held to is that the condition is about the counter the loop carries, which is what an unrecovered merge would lose.

cases.name: eval_switch_arith
cases.source: int32_t eval_switch_arith(int32_t op, int32_t a, int32_t b)

cases.name: eval_switch_sparse
cases.comment: Lowered by the compiler to arithmetic over a packed table rather than a branch per case, so there is no switch in the machine code to recover. Held only to being goto-free and correctly typed.

cases.name: eval_vec3_dot
cases.source: int32_t eval_vec3_dot(const Vec3* v, const Vec3* w)

cases.name: eval_array_max
cases.source: int32_t eval_array_max(const int32_t* arr, size_t n)

cases.name: eval_call_chain
cases.comment: helper_double and helper_triple are static and inlined at -O1, so the correct decompilation is the folded arithmetic (x * 6) with no call at all. Requiring a call here would be requiring a wrong answer.

cases.name: eval_indirect_binop
cases.source: int32_t eval_indirect_binop(int32_t op, int32_t a, int32_t b)

cases.name: eval_cmp_signed
cases.comment: The middle of the three-way compare is a cset: one of the two results is the comparison itself, used as a 0/1 value, and there is no branch in the machine code to recover. Returning the comparison says that in one line; spelling it as a second if that returns 1 or 0 is longer and no clearer.

cases.name: eval_nested
cases.source: int32_t eval_nested(int32_t a, int32_t b, int32_t c)

cases.name: eval_early_return
cases.comment: Two of the three guards end the same way, so the compiler emitted one shared tail and there is a single block with two predecessors. One goto to it is the faithful reading: xdec emits every block exactly once, which is what lets the output be checked against a disassembler, and buying a goto back by duplicating the tail would give that up.

cases.name: eval_state_machine
cases.comment: Every way out of the dispatch loop is a return or a jump past it, so the loop itself has no condition to check -- while (true) is the honest spelling, and a case coming back around is a continue.

cases.name: eval_types_struct_arg
cases.comment: The base case for the whole track, and an A/B against eval_vec3_dot, which is the same shape with no header to import. Baseline can prove a pointer and the width behind it; only the header can say the three words are x, y and z.

cases.name: eval_types_struct_field
cases.source: int32_t eval_types_struct_field(const EvalNode* node) -- reads node->left->weight
cases.comment: Two hops. The second one is the test: `left` is a pointer field, so naming it types the value it loaded, and the access through that value is nameable in turn. Without that carry the output stops at one level and reverts to offsets.

cases.name: eval_types_enum_switch
cases.source: int32_t eval_types_enum_switch(EvalKind kind, int32_t a, int32_t b)
cases.comment: An enum is a 32-bit integer to the machine and a set of names to a reader. The case labels stay numeric -- the switch is over a value, not over a declaration, and rewriting 0x1 as EVAL_KIND_SUM is a claim about which enum this integer belongs to that the parameter's type alone does not license for arbitrary arithmetic on it.

cases.name: eval_types_typedef_chain
cases.source: SizeTy eval_types_typedef_chain(const uint8_t* data, SizeTy n) -- SizeTy is size_t
cases.comment: Two typedefs deep: SizeTy names size_t, which names a 64-bit unsigned. Inference reaches the last of those and can never reach the first two, and the definition emitted for it says `typedef size_t SizeTy` rather than expanding size_t -- the platform's header owns that name.

cases.name: eval_types_fn_ptr
cases.source: int32_t eval_types_fn_ptr(EvalBinOp op, int32_t a, int32_t b) -- returns op(a, b), a tail call through the parameter
cases.comment: Arity, not spelling, over a tail call. `br x0` is read as a call through the caller's pointer (recover-tailcall), so both modes get a call and a return; the arity is then the same story as any indirect call. With no declaration every one of the eight argument registers might be an argument, so the call passes eight and the enclosing signature grows to match. The header says two, and saying so before argument recovery runs is what makes both the call and the signature come out right. The baseline return is a machine word because a tail call hands back whatever the callee left in x0 and nothing here narrows it.

cases.name: eval_types_return_struct
cases.source: EvalVec3 eval_types_return_struct(int32_t x, int32_t y, int32_t z) -- 12 bytes, returned in x0 and x1
cases.comment: A struct returned by value does not fit the recovered shape and must not be forced into it: the body hands back registers, so declaring EvalVec3 would produce C that does not compile. The header's claim goes in a comment beside the type that is true. The third component travels in x1 and is not recovered at all, which is the return-register modelling limit rather than anything type import can fix.

cases.name: eval_types_extern_global
cases.source: uint64_t eval_types_extern_global(uint64_t add) -- reads and writes extern EvalStats g_eval_stats
cases.comment: A global reached through the GOT: the relocation names the symbol, so the slot is called ptr_g_eval_stats in both modes. Typing it is not done -- the slot would have to be declared as EvalStats* and the load through it would have to stop being a dereference, together, or the output stops compiling. Until then the header adds nothing here, which is what this case records.

cases.name: eval_types_void_ptr
cases.comment: The one place inference is more specific than the header: the body reads bytes through buf, so baseline recovers uint8_t* where the declaration says void*. The header still wins, because void* is what every caller was compiled against, and the byte reads are visible in the body either way.

cases.name: eval_svc_write
cases.source: long eval_svc_write(const void* buf, unsigned long n) -- svc #0, x8=64
cases.comment: The base case for the whole track. write takes three arguments, so the three registers the source never set must come off the call, and the name must be the kernel's rather than a number.

cases.name: eval_svc_gettimeofday
cases.source: int eval_svc_gettimeofday(void* tv, void* tz) -- svc #0, x8=169
cases.comment: Two pointer arguments whose types the syscall table knows. Casting to them is what turns two 64-bit registers into an argument list a reader can check against the man page.

cases.name: eval_svc_getpid
cases.comment: getpid reads nothing, so every argument register comes off and the call prints empty. The clearest single check that arity trimming happened at all.

cases.name: eval_svc_unknown
cases.comment: A number no kernel defines. The number is printed and nothing is invented; the six raw registers stay, because with an unknown callee any of them might be an argument, and that is also why the recovered signature has six parameters rather than the source's one.

cases.name: eval_svc_nr_from_arg
cases.source: long eval_svc_nr_from_arg(long nr, long a0) -- svc #0, x8 from a parameter
cases.comment: The number is this function's argument, so it cannot be known from the function alone. What must survive is that the instruction is still recognised as a syscall and the expression that produced the number is still printed -- degrading, not guessing.

cases.name: eval_svc_errno
cases.source: long eval_svc_errno(const void* buf, unsigned long n) -- write, then a sign test
cases.comment: The idiom at every real syscall site: the kernel returns -errno, so the caller tests the sign. Here it is written plainly, and it must read as one comparison; B4 is about the obfuscated form of the same test.

cases.name: eval_svc_openat
cases.source: long eval_svc_openat(const char* path, long flags) -- svc #0, x8=56
cases.comment: aarch64 has no bare __NR_open; every open a reversed binary makes is this number with AT_FDCWD folded in, so this is the raw form the env-collection cases' libc open() calls resolve to underneath.

cases.name: eval_svc_read
cases.source: long eval_svc_read(long fd, void* buf, unsigned long n) -- svc #0, x8=63
cases.comment: Three arguments, the same shape as write with the direction reversed -- the pair that between them cover the two syscalls every /proc read in source_env.c goes through.

cases.name: eval_svc_close
cases.comment: A single descriptor argument, so five of six registers come off the call -- the trim check for a different arity than getpid's zero.

cases.name: eval_svc_mmap
cases.source: void* eval_svc_mmap(void* addr, unsigned long len, long prot, long flags, long fd, long off) -- svc #0, x8=222
cases.comment: Six arguments, the widest register set a syscall uses on this ABI -- the case that proves the wrapper chain carries x0..x5 through without dropping the last one.

cases.name: eval_svc_clock_gettime
cases.source: long eval_svc_clock_gettime(long clk_id, void* ts) -- svc #0, x8=113
cases.comment: The anti-debug timing probe's raw form: an int and a pointer, same two-argument shape as gettimeofday but a different number and a different struct.

cases.name: eval_svc_ptrace
cases.source: long eval_svc_ptrace(long request, long pid, void* addr, void* data) -- svc #0, x8=117
cases.comment: The anti-debugger's own syscall, spelled without the libc wrapper a tracer could breakpoint; the table lists it by arity only, so no argument gets a type it was never given.

cases.name: eval_svc_getuid
cases.comment: No arguments, same trim as getpid but a different number -- the check that the table is actually being read per-number rather than a name assumed from arity alone.

cases.name: eval_svc_nanosleep
cases.source: long eval_svc_nanosleep(const void* req, void* rem) -- svc #0, x8=101
cases.comment: The raw form of the sleep an anti-emulation probe times; two pointer arguments the table already knows the struct for.

cases.name: eval_svc_gettimeofday_errno
cases.source: int eval_svc_gettimeofday_errno(void* tv, void* tz) -- svc #0, x8=169, then errno store
cases.comment: The sub_199214 shape, but the value entering the errno store is a raw syscall's own result rather than a libc call's: this is the case that proves the errno-fold idiom applies to a recovered `sys_gettimeofday(...)` exactly as it does to any other call.

cases.name: eval_svc_gettimeofday_libc
cases.source: int eval_svc_gettimeofday_libc(void* tv, void* tz) -- the same operation through libc's own gettimeofday()
cases.comment: The counterpart to eval_svc_gettimeofday_errno: the identical operation, called the ordinary way, so the raw-syscall form and the PLT-resolved form sit side by side under the same category.

cases.name: eval_tailcall_table
cases.source: int32_t eval_tailcall_table(const EvalTailOp* ops, int32_t index, int32_t a, int32_t b) -- returns ops[index](a, b)
cases.comment: A tail call through a pointer read out of an array the caller passed. `-O1` emits `ldr x4,[x0,index,lsl#3]; br x4`, which is the jump-table shape with the base in a register instead of in the instruction stream -- and that difference is the whole decision: nothing in this image says what is in the caller's array, so the branch leaves. Before recover-tailcall this failed the decompilation outright. The call still passes eight registers because no declaration says otherwise; eval_types_fn_ptr is where a header cuts that down.

cases.name: eval_tailcall_import
cases.source: ssize_t eval_tailcall_import(int32_t fd, const void* buf, size_t n) -- returns write(fd, buf, n)
cases.comment: A tail call to another module: `b write@plt`, and the stub's own `br x17` through the GOT. The loader's account of that slot is the evidence, and the import name is what a reader needs. This used to emit two blocks under the same label and C that did not compile, because the value set read the unrelocated slot and 'resolved' the branch into the stub it was already in.

cases.name: eval_env_property_get_model
cases.comment: The device-fingerprint read every anti-emulator check starts with. baseline is scored, not typed: TargetProfile's android-ndk preset resolves the name with no --types argument.

cases.name: eval_env_property_find
cases.comment: The pointer-returning half of the property API, and an opaque struct (prop_info) declared only as a forward tag -- every call site only tests the pointer, never a field, so that is all the header needs to say.

cases.name: eval_env_open_cmdline
cases.comment: open is variadic in the header (the mode argument), so apply-types cannot trim the registers after it the way it trims a fixed-arity import -- they surface as this function's own parameters instead. That is a real, load-bearing limitation of variadic-call arity recovery, not a defect in this case, so the signature is left unchecked here rather than pinned to an artifact.

cases.name: eval_env_stat_libc
cases.comment: struct stat is forward-declared only, the same opaque-tag pattern as prop_info above: the call only tests the return value, never a field of the buffer.

cases.name: eval_env_getuid
cases.comment: Android's app-UID boundary check: the comparison against a fixed threshold instead of a plain identity return is what keeps -O1 from folding this into a tail call through the PLT stub (see the corpus file's header comment).

cases.name: eval_env_log_print
cases.comment: Variadic like open above: the format argument's trailing registers surface as this function's own parameters rather than being trimmed, so the signature is left unchecked.

cases.name: eval_env_ptrace
cases.comment: The classic anti-debug probe. The clamp idiom (rc < 0 ? -1 : 0) is computed entirely in 64-bit registers with no narrowing instruction after it -- ptrace itself returns long -- so baseline's recovered return width is 64 bits even though the C source declared int32_t; the same 'nothing here narrows it' limitation eval_types_fn_ptr's baseline case already documents for a tail call.

cases.name: eval_env_syscall_getpid
cases.comment: syscall(long, ...) is variadic, same arity-recovery limitation as open and __android_log_print above: unchecked signature.

cases.name: eval_env_mmap
cases.source: int32_t eval_env_mmap(void) -- mmap(NULL, 4096, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0) != MAP_FAILED

cases.name: eval_import_errno_call
cases.source: int32_t eval_import_errno_call(void) -- return errno; (a read, not the store idiom)
cases.comment: errno expands to *__errno_location(); this is the read half, kept separate from the write idiom eval_import_errno_fold covers so a regression in one cannot hide behind the other.

cases.name: eval_import_errno_fold
cases.source: int32_t eval_import_errno_fold(long raw_ret) -- errno = -raw_ret; return -1; (single guard)
cases.comment: The idiom docs/10-import-resolution.md's foldableErrnoCall exists for: *__errno_location() = -ret; as one statement, not two, because nothing else in this function reads the call's result.

cases.name: eval_import_errno_dispatch
cases.source: int32_t eval_import_errno_dispatch(int32_t op, long a, long b) -- a 3-arm switch, one arm through the errno store, all sharing one goto-reached exit
cases.comment: The sub_199214 shape with a real goto between the store and the label the other arms share -- load-bearing for the fold applying correctly once a merge sits nearby, not for the decline itself (that is pinned deterministically at the IL level in tests/emit/test_c_import_call.cpp, where register allocation is under the test's control).

cases.name: eval_import_stack_chk
cases.source: int32_t eval_import_stack_chk(const char* src) -- copies into and sums a local buffer, -fstack-protector-strong
cases.comment: The first of the two names analysis/noreturn.cpp's PLT-stub decoding was written to recognise (docs/10-import-resolution.md). eval/build.ps1 builds the whole corpus with -fstack-protector-strong for this case's sake; no other case in the corpus has a local array, so nothing else grew a canary.

cases.name: eval_import_abort
cases.source: void eval_import_abort(int32_t code) -- abort() when code < 0
cases.comment: The second name on the noreturn list: a guarded call, not a canary, so the only import in the corpus that resolves with no header entry backing the arity trim at all -- abort's prototype is void(void), the same as every other noreturn name here.

cases.name: eval_import_write_direct
cases.source: int32_t eval_import_write_direct(void) -- write(1, "x", 1), not in tail position
cases.comment: Shape A on its own, deliberately not a tail call: eval_tailcall_import (source_tailcall.c) is Shape C, which reduces to Shape A or B once recover-tailcall rewrites the branch, but never exercises a direct, ordinary call the way a real probe reads.

cases.name: eval_import_got_indirect
cases.source: int32_t eval_import_got_indirect(void) -- calls getpid through a volatile function-pointer global initialised to it
cases.comment: Shape B, and -- unlike eval_tailcall_import, whose Shape B is always also a tail call -- not one: an ordinary indirect call in the middle of a function that does something with the result afterwards, the shape a real function pointer to an import actually has.

cases.name: eval_import_snprintf
cases.comment: Variadic like open and __android_log_print in source_env.c: the format argument's trailing registers surface as this function's own parameters, so the signature is left unchecked.

cases.name: eval_import_memcpy
cases.source: int32_t eval_import_memcpy(void* dst, const void* src, size_t n) -- memcpy(dst, src, n); return n; (the call's own result is unused)

cases.name: eval_import_strcmp
cases.source: int32_t eval_import_strcmp(const char* a, const char* b) -- strcmp(a, b) == 0

cases.name: eval_import_fopen
cases.comment: FILE declared as an opaque forward tag, the same pattern as struct stat and prop_info in source_env.c: every call only passes the handle through, never reads a field of it.

cases.name: eval_jni_find_class
cases.source: jclass eval_jni_find_class(JNIEnv* env, const char* name) -- (*env)->FindClass(env, name)
cases.comment: The JNIEnv vtable call every native library's JNI_OnLoad makes first. android-ndk.hdecl carries the real jni.h table (frozen since 1.2), so the two loads this compiles to -- env's vtable pointer, then the vtable's slot 6 -- must show the real offset, 0x30, not a value invented for this corpus. Naming the call FindClass(...) itself needs the case's own signature, which zero-CLI baseline cannot supply (see docs/10-import-resolution.md); what this and its seven siblings pin is the offset math and the indirect-call recognition underneath that name.

cases.name: eval_jni_get_object_class
cases.source: jclass eval_jni_get_object_class(JNIEnv* env, jobject obj) -- (*env)->GetObjectClass(env, obj)
cases.comment: Slot 31, 0xf8 -- the call every method that only has a jobject (no class handle yet) makes before it can look anything up on it.

cases.name: eval_jni_get_method_id
cases.source: jmethodID eval_jni_get_method_id(JNIEnv* env, jclass clazz, const char* name, const char* sig) -- (*env)->GetMethodID(env, clazz, name, sig)
cases.comment: Slot 33, 0x108 -- four real arguments, so this is also the arity check: nothing here is a variadic call, and none of the eight registers may be dropped or invented.

cases.name: eval_jni_call_object_method
cases.source: jobject eval_jni_call_object_method(JNIEnv* env, jobject obj, jmethodID methodID) -- (*env)->CallObjectMethod(env, obj, methodID)
cases.comment: Slot 34, 0x110, immediately after GetMethodID's slot -- the pair every reflective call site uses back to back, so a wrong offset on either one would put them one call apart from where GetMethodID landed.

cases.name: eval_jni_call_int_method
cases.source: jint eval_jni_call_int_method(JNIEnv* env, jobject obj, jmethodID methodID) -- (*env)->CallIntMethod(env, obj, methodID)
cases.comment: Slot 49, 0x188 -- fifteen slots past CallObjectMethod, the same family with a different result width, and the one case in this group whose post-call comparison survives on its own (an int comparison, not a pointer identity) rather than needing the all-ones sentinel.

cases.name: eval_jni_new_string_utf
cases.source: jstring eval_jni_new_string_utf(JNIEnv* env, const char* bytes) -- (*env)->NewStringUTF(env, bytes)
cases.comment: Slot 167, 0x538 -- the widest gap in this group's padding (117 slots), the check that a long run of unnamed members does not throw off the count for everything declared after it.

cases.name: eval_jni_register_natives
cases.source: jint eval_jni_register_natives(JNIEnv* env, jclass clazz, const JNINativeMethod* methods, jint n) -- (*env)->RegisterNatives(env, clazz, methods, n)
cases.comment: Slot 215, 0x6b8 -- the call that binds native functions to Java method names explicitly, bypassing the export-table lookup JNI_OnLoad's implicit registration would otherwise need; a common anti-static-analysis move on its own.

cases.name: eval_jni_exception_check
cases.comment: Slot 228, 0x720 -- no arguments past env, the same arity-zero trim eval_svc_getpid checks for a syscall, here for a vtable call instead.
